questions.question: Iron and steel are ______ industries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mineral based.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron and steel industries** are **mineral-based industries**.

 
 
• Iron and steel are manufactured using **minerals **such as **iron ore**, **coal**, and **limestone**.
 
• These minerals are extracted from mines and processed to produce iron and steel.
 
• This industry is considered a **part of the heavy industry sector**, which relies heavily on mineral resources.
 
• The mineral-based nature of the iron and steel industry is reflected in its supply chain, which includes mining, transportation, and processing of minerals.
 
 
 
• **Mineral-based industries **are generally **capital-intensive **and **require large investments** in equipment and infrastructure.
 
 
• This industry **includes mining**, **processing**, and **refining **of minerals such as coal, oil, gas, and metals.
 
• It is **a critical sector for industrial development and energy production.**
 
• Some other examples of mineral based industries:
 
 
• Copper smelting industry
 
• Aluminium industry
 
• Lead and zinc smelting industry
 
• Cement industry 
 
• Fertiliser industry 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Handloom** is a **type of textile industry** that produces woven fabrics using hand-operated looms.

 
 
• It is a **labor-intensive industry** that relies on traditional techniques and skills.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture-based industries** include **food processing**, **dairy**, and **animal husbandry.**
 
 
• These industries **use agricultural products as raw materials** and involve processing, packaging, and distribution of the final products.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture **is a primary sector that **involves cultivation of crops and livestock.**
 
 
• It is a vital sector for food security and rural development.

questions.question: In India, by whom is the Chief Minister appointed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chief Minister:**

 
 
• According to Article 164 in the Indian Constitution, the Governor appoints a Chief Minister.
 
• The state's chief minister is chosen from among the **leaders of the parties that received the majority of the votes** cast in the assembly elections.
 
• The **Chief Minister has actual executive authority,** with the **Governor serving as the de facto head of state.**
 
• The **term of the Chief Minister** is not fixed and he holds office **during the pleasure of the governor.**
 
• As long as he has the backing of the majority in the legislature, the governor cannot remove him.
 
• He may also be **dismissed** by the State Legislative Assembly if a **vote of no confidence is passed** against him.
 
• A **non-legislative member** of the state legislature may be designated** as Chief Minister for a period of six months**, after which he must be elected to the state legislature, failing which he will no longer hold the position.
 
 
 
• 
 
The Governors of states:

 
 
• Governors have been discussed under Article 153 to Article 162 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India and is responsible for the administration of the state.
 
• Under Article 155, the appointment of the Governor is done by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• He/She holds office at the pleasure of the President, which means that the President can remove the Governor from office at any time without assigning any reason.
 
• The term of governor's office is normally 5 years but it can be terminated earlier.
 
• He/She can also resign from his/her office by addressing the resignation letter to the President.
 
• Under Article 157, the qualifications for appointment as a Governor are: A Governor must
 
 
• be an Indian citizen and reside in the country.
 
• attain an age of a minimum of 35 years.
 
• not be a member of both houses of the parliament and the house of the state legislature.
 
• not hold any office for generating profit.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Prime Minister:

 
• The Prime Minister of India is the head of the government at the centre.
 
• Under Article 75, he/she is appointed by the president of India if he/she has the confidence of the majority of Lok Sabha members.
 
 
• He can recommend a person's name for the post of Governor to the President.
 
• Article 74(1) states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with a Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.

questions.question: In India, the monsoon lasts for ______ days from early June to mid-September.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100 - 120.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Monsoons** are **seasonal winds** that **reverse their course** in response to the onset of a new season. 
 
• The **Arabic term** for season,** "mawsim,"** is thought to be the source of the word "monsoon."
 
• It is maintained in the region between** 20 °N and 20 °S.**
 
• **It lasts for 100–120 days, starting in early June and ending in mid-September.**
 
• India receives about **80% of its annual rainfall** during the monsoon season.
 
• In India, 64% of the population makes their living from agriculture, which is reliant on the monsoon season.
 
• Rainfall during the monsoon season replenishes reservoirs and dams, which is then utilised to produce hydroelectric power.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 

 
• **Two types** of monsoon are as follows:

 
 
• The South-west monsoon is the primary rainy season in India, which starts in June and lasts till September.

 
 
• This monsoon is caused by the differential heating of land and sea, which results in the formation of low-pressure systems over the Indian Ocean and the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• The Retreating Monsoon, also known as the North-East monsoon, brings rainfall to the southern parts of India during October and November.
 
 
• This monsoon is caused by the withdrawal of the south-west monsoon winds and the formation of a low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
 
 
• The **Indian Meteorological Department (IMD)** keeps a close eye on the start of the monsoon season to assist farmers in scheduling their farming operations.

questions.question: In which year was the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act enacted by the Central Government of India to implement the Right to Work?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __2005.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA):**

 
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was **enacted** by the Central Government of India **in the year 2005**.
 
• **Established by the Ministry of Rural Development**. 
 
• MGNREGA is one of the **biggest labor guarantee programs globally**.
 
• The **main goal **of the program is to **provide adult members of rural households** who are willing to perform unskilled manual labor related to public work with **100 days of employment guaranteed** per fiscal year.
 
• The legally-backed guarantee that any adult living in a rural area would find job **within 15 days** of requesting it, **or else a "unemployment allowance**" must be provided, is the most significant aspect of the MGNREGA framework.
 
• By giving women equal pay for equal labour, MGNREGA has been successful in lowering poverty, raising the standard of living in rural households, and empowering them.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Work:**

 
 
• It is not specifically acknowledged as a fundamental right in the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is **unenforceable in a court of law** because it is **included in Part IV of the Constitution (Directive Principles of State Policy) under Article 41.**
 
• According to **Article 41 of the Constitution**, “the State shall within the limits of its economic capacity and development, make effective provision for securing the right to work, to education and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, and in other cases of undeserved want.”

questions.question: The Government of India, by passing an Act in the year ______, revoked the special constitutional status of the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2019**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **special status, or limited autonomy, that Jammu and Kashmir** had been accorded **under Article 370** of the Indian Constitution was **removed by the Indian government on August 5, 2019.**
 
• **The President of India issued the Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order 2019 **, which e**liminated J&K's special status** and extended all of the Indian Constitution's provisions to the region.
 
• **The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019** was the name of the law that the Indian government passed which **divided the state of Jammu and Kashmir into Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir, two distinct Union Territories.**
 
• A Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court affirmed the President of India's authority to revoke Article 370 of the Indian Constitution on December 11, 2023, with a majority decision. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Article 370:**

 
• It was included in **Part XXI** of the Constitution: **"Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions."**
 
• The constitutional provision known as **Article 370 granted Jammu and Kashmir its unique status.**
 
• It **allows J&K to create its own constitution** and spares the state from the provisions of the Indian Constitution (except from Article 370 and Article 1).
 
• It** limits Parliament's ability **to enact laws pertaining to J&K and requires just "consultation" with the state government in order **to extend a central law** on topics **covered by the Instrument of Accession (IoA).**
 
• **In 1947, Governor General Lord Mountbatten and Raja Hari Singh of the then-princely state of J&K signed the IoA.**
 
• The** IoA granted Parliament the authority to enact laws only pertaining to communications, defence, and external affairs with regard to J&K.**

questions.question: Why does silver chloride turn white in sunlight?

options.text: Due to rusting of silver in the presence of oxygen
Due to decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light.
Due to displacement of silver chloride into silver oxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Due to decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silver chloride** is a **photosensitive compound**, which means it reacts to light by decomposing.
 
• When silver chloride is exposed to sunlight, the **energy from the light** causes the** compound to break down into silver and chlorine ions.**
 
• The s**ilver ions combine with other substances** in the environment to **form a white precipitate**, which gives the **appearance of the silver chloride turning white**.
 
• This process is reversible, and the white precipitate can turn back into silver chloride when removed from sunlight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Application of this phenomenon**:

 
 
• As this process is reversible, as the grey color can fade when the silver chloride is shielded from light or heated.
 
• This property has **historical significance in photography**, as it was **used in the early photographic process known as the daguerreotype**.
 
 
 
• **Redox reaction:**
 
 
• **Redox reactions are chemical processes involving oxidation and reduction in which the oxidation states of the reactants change.** 
 
• In a chemical reaction, the **material that is being reduced **is referred to as the** oxidizing agent**, and the **substance that is being oxidized** is referred to as the **reducing agent**. 
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction:**
 
 
• **When an atom in a molecule is displaced by another atom, this is known as a displacement reaction.**

questions.question: In which year was the Depressed Classes Association founded by B.R. Ambedkar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1930.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **BR Ambedkar** **founded **the **Depressed Classes Association (DCA) on July 23, 1930**, in **Bombay (now Mumbai).**
 
• It was formed** to fight for the rights of the Scheduled Castes/Dalits (formerly known as untouchables)**, who were oppressed and discriminated against by the upper caste.
 
• It was involved in the meetings with Lord Irwin and demanded a provision for separate electorates in India for the depressed classes.
 
• It later became the **Scheduled Castes Federation in 1942** and then the **Republican Party of India in 1957.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. Bhim Rao Ambedkar:**

 
 
• He was a prominent Indian **jurist**, **economist**,** social reformer**, and **politician**.
 
• He was **born **on **April 14, 1891 in Mhow, Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• In 1924, he started an Association for the welfare of the depressed classes and in **1927**, he **started the Bahishkrit Bharat newspaper **to address the cause of the depressed classes.
 
• He led the **Mahad Satyagraha in March 1927.**
 
• **He **and **Mahatma Gandhi signed the Poona Pact in 1932,** giving up on the notion of separate electorates for the lower classes (**Communal Award).**
 
• In order to protect the interests of the downtrodden classes, he founded the **Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha (1923)**, the **Independent Labour Party in 1936, **and the** Scheduled Castes Federation (1942).**
 
• He was the **Chairman of the Drafting Committee** and is remembered as the **"Father of the Indian Constitution."**
 
• In **1947**, Dr. Ambedkar **became Minister of Law in the first Cabinet** of independent India.
 
• He passed away on **December 6, 1956**, which is commemorated as** Mahaparinirvan Diwas.** His memorial is known as **Chaitya Bhoomi**, located **in Mumbai**.
 
• He was also awarded India’s highest civilian honour the **Bharat Ratna in 1990.**
 
• Journals and books by him:
 
 
• Journals - **Mooknayak **(1920), **Bahishkrit Bharat** (1927), **Samatha **(1929), Janata (1930).
 
• Books - **The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Solution** (1923), **The Annihilation of Caste** (1936), **Thoughts on Pakistan** (1940), Mr. Gandhi and Emancipation of Untouchables (1943), **Pakistan or Partition of India** (1945), Who were the Shudras (1948), **Buddha or Karl Marx** (1956), The Rise and Fall of Hindu Women.

questions.question: According to Chola inscriptions, what was the land for maintaining schools called?
questions.solution:
સાચો જવાબ __શાલભોગ__ છે. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The following land classifications are mentioned in the Chola inscriptions:

 
 

 **devdan**
 Land granted to temples and religious institutions.
 
 

 **Shalbhogh**
 **Land granted for maintenance of schools.**
 
 

 **Brahmadeya**
 A type of land granted to Brahmins or priests.
 
 

 **Vellanavagai**
 Property/land owned by a non-Brahmin cultivator or soldier.
 
 

 **Pallicchandam**
 Land donated to Jain institutions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Chola Dynasty:

 
• One of the longest dynasties to rule the **southern parts of India is the Chola (8th-12th century CE).**
 
• It was founded by Vijayalaya.
 
• He defeated the Pallavas in the 9th century, and his reign officially began. Until the 13th century, this rule was in force for more than five centuries.
 
• In this dynasty, **Rajaraja Chola** was one of the most powerful rulers.
 
 
• He was the first person to visit the banks of the river Ganges.
 
• He got fame as the** conqueror of Ganges.**
 
• This period is known as the Golden Age of Cholas.
 
 
 
• Chola temples like Brihadeswara Temple, Rajarajeswara Temple and Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple took the Dravidian style of architecture to new heights.
 
• Nataraja in Tandava dance posture is an important example of Chola sculpture.
 
• **Chola Inscriptions:**
 
 
• Inscriptions mainly document gifts and donations made to temples by kings and other individuals. **Taxes and land transactions form an important part of their content.**
 
• Political edicts are written on **copper plates** in addition to** stone inscriptions.**
 
• The Uttaramairur inscription details the elections to the local self-governing bodies, which were announced by Prantaka Chola.

questions.question: What is the major component of cellular energy transfer systems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Phosphorus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phosphorus is an essential component of ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**, which is the molecule **used by cells to store and transfer energy.**
 
• **ATP is synthesized through cellular respiration**, a process that involves a series of chemical reactions that break down glucose and other molecules to release energy.
 
• Phosphorus is also a key element in other cellular processes, such as DNA and RNA synthesis, membrane structure, and signal transduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP):**

 
 
• All living species' cells include the e**nergy-carrying chemical adenosine triphosphate (ATP).**
 
• When **food molecules break down, chemical energy is captured by ATP** and r**eleased to power other cellular functions.**
 
• For **three main purposes**, cells need chemical energy:
 
 
• To power metabolic events that wouldn't happen on their own;
 
• To move necessary materials across membranes;
 
• To perform mechanical functions like muscle movement.
 
 
 
• **It is the role of lipids and carbohydrates like glycogen to store chemical energy; ATP is not one of those molecules.**
 
• ATP is created when energy from storage molecules is required by the cell. Then, A**TP acts as a shuttle, carrying energy** to areas of the cell where energy-intensive processes are occurring.

• **Sajibu Cheiraoba:**

 
 
• Every year, **in Manipur**, Sajibu Cheiraoba is celebrated at the** end of March or the beginning of April**.
 
• Ritual performances are held to commemorate the occasion and bring good fortune for the coming year. 
 
• The **Cheiraoba festival marks the beginning of a new year based on the lunar calendar** and mathematical computations related to the customs and **cultural legacy of the Meitei community in India**.
 
• The** first day of the first month in the Meitei calendar Sajibu is Sajibu Nongma Pānba, sometimes referred to as Meetei Cheiraoba.**
 
• The **Meitei deity Lainingthou Sanamahi **receives ceremonial morning offerings of fruits, vegetables, rice, and other raw foods on the first day of the new year.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****Sanamahism:**

 
 
• The **Meitei faith's most revered deity, God Lainingthou Sanamahi**, is the inspiration behind the name of this **polytheistic religion.**
 
• The superior deity Leimarel Sidabi and the supreme god Yaibirel Sidaba, also called Saalailel Sidaba, are the parents of Sanamahi, the eldest son.
 
• It is an **indigenous religion practiced by the Meitei community in Manipur.**

questions.question: What is the full form of NABARD?

options.text: National Bank for Agriculture and River Development
National Bank for Architecture and Rural Development
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
National Body for Agriculture and Rural Development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NABARD** is the acronym used for **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.**
 
• NABARD:
 
 
• India's top development bank, NABARD, aims to support fair and sustainable rural and agricultural development.
 
• As per the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981, it is a statutory body that was founded in 1982 by Parliament.
 
• Its headquarter is located in Mumbai, India.
 
• It **supervises Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Cooperative Banks**, assisting them in establishing safe banking procedures and integrating them with the CBS (Core Banking Solution) system.
 
• It offers financing assistance for the construction of rural infrastructure.
 
• It creates credit strategies at the district level to direct and inspire the banking sector to meet these goals.
 
• Current Chairman of NABARD is Shri. Shaji K V
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sivaraman Committee:**

 
 
• In response to pressure from the Indian government, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI) established the Committee to Review the Arrangements for Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development (CRAFICARD) in 1979.**
 
• **Former Planning Commission member Shri B. Sivaraman** served as the **committee's chairman.**
 
• The **Committee's report from 1979** stated that a new organizational mechanism was required to give credit-related concerns associated with rural development the focused attention, firm guidance, and undivided attention they require.
 
• As a result, the **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was established in 1982 as a statutory organization.**​

questions.question: Who among the following has been awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Kathak?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Sunaina Hazarilal:**

 
 
• Indian classical dancer Sunayana Hazarilal Agarwal is renowned for her proficiency in the **Kathak classical dance** style. 
 
• She is purportedly the **last living practitioner of the Janakiprasad Gharana of Kathak, popularly referred to as the Banares Gharana**. 
 
• In** 2011**, the Indian government bestowed upon her the **Padma Shri,** the fourth highest civilian honor.
 
• **The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award winner (2003)**, among other honors
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award:**
 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi,** India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama**, bestows the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award,** also called the Akademi Puraskar.** 
 
• It is the greatest honor bestowed upon those involved in the performing arts in India.
 
• **1952 marked its initial awarding**.
 
 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form of North India basically Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
• It is a storytelling dance that involves intricate footwork, spins, and graceful movements of the hands and arms.
 
• The themes of Kathak are often romantic or devotional in nature.

• A **Sattriya dancer** from Assam.

• An Indian classical dancer associated with S**attriya dance.**
 
• Awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2019**.
 
 
 
• **Jogen Dutta**:
 
 
• He is a well-known **Khol player **and percussionist from Assam.
 
• He became a well-known artist and **guru of Sattriya Nrittya** and other Assamese neo-Vaishnavite art forms.

questions.question: The principle of fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution has been taken from which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights in the Constitution of India are enshrined in **Part III ****(Article 12-35)** of the Constitution, which **guarantees civil liberties such as freedom of speech, religion, and equality before the law.**
 
• These **Fundamental Rights were inspired by the Bill of Rights of the United States Constitution**, **which was adopted in 1791**. The Indian Constitution borrowed heavily from the US Constitution, which is why it is often called a 'bag of borrowings.'
 
• The Indian Constitution also drew inspiration from the Constitution of Ireland, which was adopted in 1937 and provided for fundamental rights and freedoms.
 
• The Constitution of India also borrowed from the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 1948.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__ **List of Borrowed Features of Indian Constitution:**
